places.name: Sydney Harbour Bridge Climb

places.name: Darling Harbour Dinner
places.description: Dine at a waterfront restaurant overlooking the illuminated harbour and city lights.

places.name: Trevi Fountain & Spanish Steps
places.description: Toss a coin into the world-famous Baroque fountain and walk the historic 135-step staircase.

places.name: Trastevere Food & Wine Walk
places.description: Wander cobblestone alleyways savoring authentic carbonara, supplì, and local Roman gelato.

places.name: Pantheon & Piazza Navona
places.description: Marvel at the world's largest unreinforced concrete dome and Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers.

places.name: Sagrada Família Basilica

places.name: Rijksmuseum & Museumplein
places.description: Admire Rembrandt's Night Watch and world-class Dutch Master masterpieces in grand halls.

places.name: Jordaan Canal Boat Cruise
places.description: Glide along UNESCO-listed 17th-century canals past gabled merchant houses and houseboats.

places.name: De Pijp Food Tour & Stroopwafels
places.description: Sample warm gooey Dutch stroopwafels, bitterballen, and artisan craft cheeses.

places.name: Fushimi Inari Taisha (Torii Gates)
places.description: Hike through thousands of vermilion torii gates winding up the sacred Mount Inari.

places.name: Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion)

places.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove & Tenryu-ji
places.description: Stroll amidst towering green bamboo stalks followed by UNESCO temple gardens and matcha.

places.name: Brandenburg Gate & Reichstag

places.name: East Side Gallery & Spree Walk

places.name: Kreuzberg Street Food & Craft Beer
places.description: Taste Berlin currywurst, authentic doner kebabs, and local craft brews in a trendy district.

places.name: Ponte Vecchio Sunset & Gelato

rome: Book Colosseum and Vatican tickets at least 3 weeks ahead online.
Dress respectfully when entering churches (knees and shoulders covered).
Drink from the 'nasoni' public drinking fountains — the water is cold and clean.
Avoid eating right next to major monuments where prices are inflated.
barcelona: Book Sagrada Família and Park Güell in advance; tickets sell out days early.
Beware of pickpockets on Las Ramblas and in crowded metro stations.
Lunch is usually served 1:30–3:30pm and dinner doesn't start until 8:30–9pm.
Buy a T-Casual 10-trip card for convenient metro and bus travel.
amsterdam: Always look both ways for cyclists before crossing — bike paths are serious business.
Buy museum tickets (Anne Frank, Van Gogh) weeks in advance.
Rent a bicycle to explore the city like a local.
Public transit takes contactless debit/credit cards directly at the turnstiles.
kyoto: Visit Fushimi Inari at dawn (6:00–7:00 AM) to experience the gates without crowds.
Be respectful of geishas and maikos in Gion — photograph from a polite distance.
Carry cash for temple admissions as many do not accept credit cards.
Take local buses or rent an e-bike to navigate Kyoto's flat temple districts.
berlin: Get a 24-hour or 7-day BVG transit pass for unlimited U-Bahn, S-Bahn, and trams.
Always validate your train ticket at the yellow/red stamp boxes before boarding.
Carry cash — many independent cafes, bars, and food stalls do not take cards.
Most retail shops and supermarkets are strictly closed on Sundays.
florence: Florence is very compact — walk everywhere instead of taking taxis.
Reserve entry for the Uffizi and Accademia well in advance to skip hours of queues.
Head to Piazzale Michelangelo for the finest sunset panorama over the city.
Try the Florentine steak (Bistecca alla Fiorentina) at a traditional trattoria.
zurich: Water from the city's 1,200 public fountains is 100% pure Alpine drinking water.
Use the Zurich Card for free public transit and admission to top museums.
Swiss public trains run with minute-precise punctuality — never be late.
Many shops close by 6:30 or 7:00 PM and remain closed all day Sunday.
lombok: Rent a scooter to explore the south coast beaches around Kuta Lombok.
Bring cash for local warungs and beach parking attendants.
Respect local Islamic Sasak customs and dress modestly when outside beach areas.
Take fast boats between the Gili Islands and Bangsal Harbour.
bali: Carry small cash for temple donations and local markets.
Wear a sarong when visiting temples — many provide them at the entrance.
Book sunrise hikes to Mount Batur at least a day in advance.
Try local warungs for authentic and affordable Balinese food.
jakarta: Use Gojek or Grab apps for affordable transport around the city.
Avoid driving during peak hours (7-9am, 5-8pm) — traffic is severe.
Bargain at traditional markets but pay fixed prices at malls.
Stay hydrated — Jakarta is hot and humid year-round.
yogyakarta: Hire a local guide for Borobudur — they bring the history to life.
Visit Borobudur at sunrise for the best light and fewer crowds.
Try gudeg (jackfruit stew) — the signature dish of Yogyakarta.
Bargain respectfully at Malioboro, prices are usually negotiable.
tokyo: Get a Suica or Pasmo IC card for easy train and bus travel.
Many restaurants don't accept credit cards — carry yen.
Visit popular spots early in the morning to avoid crowds.
Download Google Translate with the Japanese offline pack.
paris: Book Eiffel Tower and Louvre tickets online well in advance.
Validate your metro ticket before boarding every single time.
Restaurants are usually closed between 2pm–7pm — plan meals accordingly.
A simple 'Bonjour' and 'Merci' go a long way with locals.
london: Get an Oyster card or use contactless to pay for the Tube and buses.
Many world-class museums (British Museum, Natural History) are free.
Carry an umbrella — London weather is famously unpredictable.
Book popular restaurants and attractions well ahead, especially weekends.
singapore: Singapore's MRT is one of the world's best — use it everywhere.
Hawker centres are the best value food in the city, from S$3–8 a dish.
Chewing gum is banned — don't bring it in.
Download the MyTransport.SG app for real-time bus arrival times.
bangkok: Take the BTS Skytrain or MRT to avoid Bangkok's notorious traffic jams.
Always negotiate tuk-tuk fares before you get in.
Dress modestly when visiting temples — shoulders and knees must be covered.
Eat where the locals eat — street food stalls are cheap and delicious.
seoul: Get a T-money card for seamless subway and bus travel.
Download Naver Maps — Google Maps coverage is limited in Korea.
Convenience stores (CU, GS25) serve surprisingly good and cheap hot food.
Visit Gyeongbokgung in hanbok for free entry — rentals are nearby.
dubai: Dress modestly in traditional souks and public places.
The Dubai Metro is clean, cheap, and has women-only carriages.
Book the desert safari through a reputable agency to avoid scams.
Carry cash for souks but cards are accepted almost everywhere else.
new york: Get a MetroCard or tap your contactless card on the subway — it's the fastest way around.
Many top museums offer free or pay-what-you-wish entry on certain evenings.
Walk between nearby attractions — NYC is very walkable in good weather.
Book popular restaurants weeks in advance, especially for weekends.
sydney: Get an Opal card for trains, buses, and ferries across the network.
The Bondi to Coogee coastal walk is free and absolutely stunning.
Book Harbour Bridge Climb months ahead — it sells out fast.
Australian sun is extremely strong — wear SPF 50+ sunscreen.
default: Research local customs and etiquette before your trip.
Keep digital copies of important documents in the cloud.
Pack a portable charger — you'll use your phone a lot.
Learn a few basic phrases in the local language.
